judge_assessment.explanation: I independently recomputed all twelve results and they are correct: 18/60 = 30%, 21/25 = 84%, 40% of 30 = 12, 36/45 = 80%, 15% of 120 = 18, 45/250 = 18%, 3% of 200 = 6, (300-250)/250 = 20%, 5.40/80 = 6.75%, 62% of 250 = 155, (96-72)/96 = 25%, and 168/1.20 = 140. The judge's specific claim about 'the 20-percent membership increase reversal' is exact: problem 12 gives the new total, not the added part, and the verify entry solves 120n/100 = 168 rather than 20n/100 = 168. The 'extraction noise' the judge worked around is only pdftotext flattening the displayed proportion; there really are twelve problems. I also checked what the judge did not state: every problem has exactly one printed answer slot and exactly one verify entry, nothing on the sheet asks for an explanation or a drawing so the claim of zero manual items is truthful, all six study-guide checks recompute correctly (60%, 85%, 80, 75, 15%, 20%), the standard tag '6.RP.A.3.c / 7.RP.A.3' matches both the task contract and the standards-map row for percent problems, and every Quick Answers entry is numeric so none of the bank's rendering failure modes is triggered. I found no defect to report.

strengths_to_preserve: Two worked models sit at the head of the sheet using the SAME three numbers (27, 45, 60) with the unknown in different positions, closing with 'Same three numbers, different unknown - read carefully which one is missing.' That single design choice is what makes the whole sheet about identifying the missing quantity rather than about arithmetic.

Problems 8 and 12 are a deliberate pair: 8 gives the original and the new value and asks for the rate, 12 gives the rate and the new value and asks for the original, with the stem's parenthetical naming the trap ('168 is not the part that was added - it is the new whole, which is 120% of last year's membership').

Problem 9's decimal part (5.40 of 80) is verified with an approx entry rather than an exact eval, which is the right type for a money-derived rate, and its declared trap (1481.48 from inverting part and whole) is machine-checked as distinguishably wrong.

The study guide's watch-out block ends on the reversal rule stated as a procedure - 'After a 20% increase, the new total is 120% of the old one, so undo it by dividing by 1.20 - never by taking 20% off the new total' - which is exactly the reasoning problem 12 demands.
case_summary: The cleanest case in this shard and a correct ACCEPT. All twelve percent results and all six study-guide checks recompute correctly; the ramp runs 1 to 5 through rate, whole, and percent change; the part-over-whole equals percent-over-100 relationship is stated once and used in every solution with the missing quantity named on the first line. Verification is complete rather than merely green: one printed answer slot per problem, one verify entry per slot, no open response anywhere on the sheet so the zero-manual claim is honest, correct in-band standard tags, and an all-numeric Quick Answers bank that avoids the renderer defects that hurt other cases in this run. Nothing here needs fixing.
